items.title: NVDA Stock: Where Compounding Could Take The Price
items.summary: This is no longer just a chip company; it is becoming the central bank for the AI revolution. NVIDIA is helping establish financing platforms to raise over $500 billion of third-party capital for its customers. It has also directly invested nearly $50 billion in the Frontier AI labs, effectively underwriting its own demand.

items.title: Marvell's Hyperscaler Deal Lands In A Fiscal Year Management Will Not Size Yet
items.summary: The programs the deal covers in the near term were already inside the targets management had published, and it is connectivity rather than custom silicon that management points to for the raise that did arrive.

items.title: Stocks to Watch Recap: Amazon, PG&E, Nvidia, Chevron
items.summary: ↘️ Amazon (AMZN): Shares fell about 2.5% after The Wall Street Journal reported that the Federal Trade Commission planned to file a lawsuit against the ecommerce giant. The FTC filed its suit later Monday.

items.title: The Biggest Risk To Cerebras Systems Stock Is Sitting Inside Its Backlog
items.summary: The order book that makes Cerebras look de-risked came from a single deal, and the hyperscaler partnerships meant to broaden it are not yet producing revenue.

items.title: Is Broadcom (AVGO) Stock a Buy Before Its Q3 Earnings?
items.summary: Broadcom is scheduled to report results for its fiscal third quarter after-market hours on Wednesday, September 2, with Wall Street looking for another quarter of exceptional growth.

items.title: Top Analyst Reports for Microsoft, Intel & Bank of America
items.summary: Microsoft's AI momentum and Azure expansion support growth, while capacity constraints and competition remain key challenges ahead.

items.title: Intel Stock Is Paying Now For Revenue Due Later
items.summary: Intel's capital spending keeps climbing while outside customers still contribute almost none of the foundry's revenue, and that gap is the main risk in the stock.

items.title: The Floor Under Micron's Worst Case Is Written Into Its Contracts, Not Memory Prices
items.summary: The take-or-pay agreements that bears read as a cap on upside are the same ones that put a priced floor under Micron's worst case.
